title: Math Foundations & Research Habits
focus: Review vectors, matrices, tensor shapes, and the chain rule; establish habits for reading papers and logging experiments.
deliverable: Submit a one-page math self-assessment, derive the gradients of a two-layer MLP by hand, and write a reading note using the Problem / Method / Evidence / Limitations template.

title: Probability, Losses & Optimization
focus: Connect MLE, cross-entropy, and KL divergence; understand SGD, AdamW, and generalization, and distinguish the roles of training, validation, and test sets.
deliverable: Explain the difference between cross-entropy and KL divergence with a numerical example. Plot loss curves for two optimizers and record random seeds and data splits.

title: Build a Reproducible Training Loop
focus: Learn tensors, Autograd, DataLoader, checkpoints, and basic debugging; use Git to manage experiments.
deliverable: Build training and validation loops in native PyTorch, demonstrate checkpoint recovery, and provide run commands, configurations, and logs.

title: Neural Networks & Your First Ablation
focus: Understand activations, initialization, normalization, residual connections, and regularization; build intuition for CNNs and recurrent networks.
deliverable: Change one factor at a time on the same small dataset to compare the effects of normalization or residual connections. Submit learning curves and failure cases.

title: Understand Q, K & V
focus: Derive scaled dot-product attention and understand multi-head attention, self-attention, cross-attention, and causal/padding masks.
deliverable: Implement masked multi-head attention from scratch, annotate tensor shapes at each step, and explain why attention scores are divided by √dₖ.

title: Assemble a Transformer Block
focus: Connect attention, FFNs, normalization, and positional encoding; understand the KV cache, prefill/decode, and computational costs.
deliverable: Implement a Transformer block and verify mask behavior. Use a diagram to explain the computation saved and GPU memory added by the KV cache, and explain MHA / MQA / GQA.

title: Language Model Data & Objectives
focus: Understand tokenization, next-token loss, perplexity, and data cleaning; compare GPT, BERT, and encoder-decoder models.
deliverable: Prepare a small corpus with documented sources, check for train/test duplicates, and demonstrate minimal examples of tokenization, packing, and causal language modeling loss.

title: Train a Mini-GPT
focus: Complete small-scale autoregressive training and generation, compare sampling strategies, and discuss scaling laws and compute budgets.
deliverable: Submit a runnable Mini-GPT, validation perplexity, and a comparison of greedy, temperature, and top-p generation. Document training costs and limitations.

title: Low-Rank Adaptation & Fine-Tuning
focus: Understand LoRA's low-rank updates, initialization, insertion points, and merging; compare full fine-tuning, LoRA, and QLoRA.
deliverable: Implement a LoRA linear layer from scratch, check the trainable parameter count and equivalence after merging, and compare at least two ranks under fixed settings.

title: Sparse Experts & Routing
focus: Understand routers, top-k routing, load balancing, and capacity; distinguish total parameters from active parameters.
deliverable: Implement a simplified MoE layer with 4 experts, plot the token routing distribution, and compare expert collapse with and without load balancing.

title: From Images to Visual Representations
focus: Connect CNNs, ResNets, and ViTs; understand patch embeddings, data augmentation, and global versus local features.
deliverable: Annotate CNN and ViT feature shapes, compare global and patch representations of the same image, and describe how detection, segmentation, and classification outputs differ.

title: Image-Text Alignment & Self-Supervision
focus: Understand how the objectives of InfoNCE, CLIP, SigLIP, and DINO differ, and learn the uses of SAM / SAM2.
deliverable: Perform zero-shot classification with pretrained CLIP, compare two prompt sets, report accuracy and failure cases, and explain the training objectives of CLIP and DINO.

title: Latent Variables & VAEs
focus: Understand the ELBO, reparameterization, and KL regularization; compare AEs, VAEs, β-VAEs, and VQ-VAEs.
deliverable: Train a VAE on MNIST, show reconstructions, random samples, and latent interpolations, and log the reconstruction loss and KL term separately.

title: Diffusion & Generative Processes
focus: Learn diffusion's forward noising, denoising, noise schedules, and CFG; explore Flow Matching mathematics and implementation as an optional extension.
deliverable: Diagram DDPM training and sampling, and explain ε / x₀ / v prediction. Optionally implement diffusion or Flow Matching on a 2D toy distribution, depending on your compute budget.

title: Connect Vision & Language
focus: Understand how vision encoders, projectors, Q-Formers, and LLMs connect, along with visual alignment and instruction tuning.
deliverable: Diagram the complete data flow from an input image to an answer in LLaVA or Qwen2.5-VL, annotate shapes at each layer, and compare the model with CLIP.

title: Multimodal Evaluation & Failure Analysis
focus: Understand dynamic resolution, visual tokens, video inputs, and visual hallucinations; design a small evaluation with traceable records.
deliverable: Curate a small example set covering VQA, OCR, and grounding. Record input settings and outputs, identify at least three failure categories, and propose testable hypotheses.

title: Measure Efficiency First
focus: Distinguish FLOPs, latency, throughput, and GPU memory components; understand profiling, checkpointing, and basic parallelism strategies.
deliverable: Build a benchmark with fixed inputs and batch size. Report warmup, measurement methods, accuracy, token count, latency, and peak GPU memory.

title: Compress Models & Visual Tokens
focus: Compare quantization, distillation, pruning, token merging, and KV cache compression; analyze accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.
deliverable: Choose one compression method and compare it with the baseline using the same task, data, and evaluation settings. Plot accuracy versus latency or memory.

title: SFT & Knowledge Distillation
focus: Understand teacher forcing, exposure bias, forward/reverse KL, and the distribution differences between offline and on-policy distillation.
deliverable: Calculate both KL directions on a toy distribution, diagram how SFT and on-policy distillation produce training data, and propose settings for a fair comparison.

title: Preference Optimization & Policy Gradients
focus: Learn the basic ideas behind rewards, policy gradients, baselines, and DPO; explore PPO / GRPO / RLOO derivations as optional extensions.
deliverable: Implement REINFORCE on a toy task, compare training curves with and without a baseline, and explain RLHF / RLVR and common reward hacking problems.

title: Elective: Long Video & Memory
focus: Elective: study frame sampling, temporal representations, and memory updates. Use this week to reinforce core modules or reproduce a project if this direction is outside your focus.
deliverable: Compare two frame-sampling or memory strategies under a fixed memory budget and outline an evaluation of accuracy, memory, and latency; alternatively, submit reproduction records for a core project.

title: Elective: VLA & World Models
focus: Elective: connect MDPs / POMDPs, imitation learning, action policies, and world models. You may replace this week with deeper reading in your chosen direction.
deliverable: Diagram the observation → policy → action → environment control loop, compare approaches such as ACT, Diffusion Policy, or VLA, and design a table for rollout success rates and failure categories.

title: Define a Question & Reproduce a Baseline
focus: Form a falsifiable hypothesis in your chosen direction and define relevant baselines, data licenses, compute budgets, and evaluation protocols.
deliverable: Submit a one-page research plan, baseline reproduction results, an experiment matrix, and a resource budget. Document differences between the original paper's results and your reproduction conditions.

title: Deliver a Small Research Study
focus: Complete key ablations, validation across multiple random seeds, failure analysis, and technical writing; distinguish statistical significance from practical value.
deliverable: Deliver reproducible code, configurations, and logs; a main results table; a set of ablations; failure cases; and a short report with Method / Results / Limitations sections.
